name: Darius
overview: Darius, identified as the son of Ahasuerus and a Mede, is a male figure mentioned in Daniel 9:1. He is likely Darius I, son of Xerxes, situating him within the historical context of Persian monarchy. His role is noted within the biblical narrative as part of the Medo-Persian empire's leadership.
namesAndTitles: The name Darius means 'he who upholds the good.' It is a proper name mentioned in Daniel 9:1 and was not given by God. This meaning reflects a characteristic attributed to this ruler, though the Bible does not elaborate further on its significance.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Darius is a descendant of Ahasuerus, as stated in Daniel 9:1. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are detailed in the biblical text for this individual.
scriptureSignificance: Darius holds importance in the biblical record as a ruler during the time referenced in Daniel 9:1, marking a significant period in Israel's history under Medo-Persian dominion. His identification as the son of Ahasuerus connects him to the lineage of Persian kings, providing historical context for the prophetic and historical events unfolding in Daniel. His reign signifies the continuation of God's sovereign oversight over earthly kingdoms, fulfilling the divine purposes revealed in Scripture.
